clue.text: Father keeps children quiet with a French dog

indicators.note: a father who keeps something holds it within, so the other pieces go inside him

parts.note: dad is an everyday word for father
CH is a standard abbreviation for child or children
sh is the call for quiet
un is French for a

explanation.surface: A dad hushes the kids while walking a dog from France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' just joins the quiet piece to the French article inside DAD.
explanation.definitionFit: The breed is a short-legged hound originally from Germany, so it is an example of a dog.

clue.text: Girl, coy and attractive

parts.note: Di is a short girl's name, as in Diana
coy means bashful or shy

explanation.surface: A young woman is described as both bashful and good-looking.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal British slang for good-looking or sexually appealing; a synonym of attractive.

clue.text: House with somewhere to sleep and creaking gate

parts.note: a cot is a small bed

indicators.note: a creaking gate is loose and out of shape, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A country home with a bed inside and a noisy garden gate.
explanation.definitionFit: A small rural dwelling is a kind of house; the definition is a broad category containing the answer.

clue.text: Sportswear on leading baseball player

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sitting on another comes above it, so it is written first

parts.note: shorts are worn for sport
being at the top means leading

explanation.surface: A star baseball player dressed in athletic kit.
explanation.definitionFit: The fielder stationed between second and third base is a specific position in baseball.

clue.text: Mourner carries something from crematorium?

indicators.note: the word Mourner carries the short vessel inside its letters

explanation.surface: A grieving person holds the ashes vessel after a cremation.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashes are returned from a crematorium in a vase-like vessel, so the question mark marks an example.

clue.text: Arrogant cur guarding tunnel leading to Ireland?

indicators.note: a guard dog wraps around what it protects, so the cur's letters surround the rest

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog

indicators.note: the tunnel comes before the island, ahead of it in order

parts.note: a mine is a tunnel dug underground
Erin is the poetic name for Ireland

explanation.surface: A snarling dog guards a passage running to the Irish coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Bossy and overbearing behaviour is close in sense to arrogant, a near synonym.

clue.text: Wine imbibed by some doctors

indicators.note: the drink is swallowed inside the words some doctors, sitting across them

explanation.surface: A few physicians are drinking claret.
explanation.definitionFit: A red wine from the Bordeaux region of France, so an example of wine.

clue.text: Fellow supervising operations research where police operate …

indicators.note: in a down clue the supervisor sits above, so the fellow is written first

parts.note: a fellow is a man

explanation.surface: A man overseeing research in a police district, run on into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: British police slang calls an officer's patch or territory their manor.

clue.text: … arrests criminal instead

indicators.note: something criminal is bent, so the word instead is twisted into new order

explanation.surface: Continuing the last clue, police hold a lawbreaker in someone else's place.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold someone in custody is to arrest them; a synonym in the verb form.

clue.text: After mass, priest boards vehicle with English friar

indicators.note: a passenger who boards a vehicle goes inside it

parts.note: a cart is a wheeled vehicle

indicators.note: the priest comes after the mass in order

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for mass in physics
Eli is the priest of the Bible who raised Samuel

explanation.surface: After Mass a cleric climbs into a car alongside an English monk.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the Order of Our Lady of Mount Carmel is a mendicant brother, i.e. a friar.

clue.text: Note start of disruption in Dover or Folkestone?

indicators.note: the opening letter is placed in the middle of the town's description

parts.note: both are towns in the south-east of England, giving SE plus town

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Write down the beginning of chaos at a Channel port.
explanation.walkthrough: Dover and Folkestone are Channel ports in Kent, south-east England, hence SE TOWN.
explanation.definitionFit: To note something is to write or record it, which is the phrasal verb's meaning.

clue.text: In back room put new computers etc and screen

indicators.note: the new computing pieces are put inside the backward room
back means the word room is read from the end

parts.note: taken as written
IT is information technology

explanation.surface: Install fresh computer kit and a display in the back office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns ROOM into MOOR before the other letters go in.
explanation.definitionFit: A computer display unit is a screen; as verbs both also mean to check or vet.

clue.text: Cause of ferment unknown to Asian countries?

parts.note: y is an unknown quantity in algebra
the East means the countries of Asia

explanation.surface: What makes things bubble is a mystery to the nations of Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: Fungal cells feeding on sugar produce fermentation, so this organism causes it.

clue.text: A US friend arranged to collect money for charity

indicators.note: the letters of the words are arranged into a new order

explanation.surface: An American pal organised a collection for a good cause.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise funds for a cause is the very meaning of the verb, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Family member waving flag endlessly in the war

indicators.note: a waving flag flutters about, so all these letters are mixed up
endlessly means the last letter of flag is dropped

explanation.surface: A relative fluttering a banner during wartime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts flag to FLA, which joins IN and THE WAR as the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A spouse's father is a relative by marriage, so he is a family member.

clue.text: Navies said to deal with press gang here, once?

parts.note: navies are fleets of ships

indicators.note: said means the words are heard rather than read

parts.note: to treat something is to deal with it

explanation.surface: Sailors press-ganging recruits in the days of naval impressment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said' covers the whole phrase: 'fleets treat' spoken sounds like the two-word answer. The 'press gang' is journalists, not naval kidnappers.
explanation.definitionFit: The London street housing the British national newspapers was where the press worked, until they moved away.

clue.text: Like small group fighting in river of Cornwall

indicators.note: the fighting is placed inside the river's name

parts.note: the Fal is a river in Cornwall, England, flowing to Falmouth
action means fighting in battle

explanation.surface: Like a band of rebels clashing in a Cornish river.
explanation.definitionFit: A faction is a small dissenting group, so the adjective describes something belonging to one.

clue.text: Princess once upset to catch beginning of this four-letter word

indicators.note: the reversed royal name catches the opening letter inside it
in a down clue upset means turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: Princess Margaret, sister of Queen Elizabeth II, who died in 2002

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A former royal is annoyed at hearing a rude four-letter word.
explanation.definitionFit: A term built of four letters, such as the Hebrew name of God, is a four-letter word.

clue.text: Short film showing runner

indicators.note: short means the word is cut back by its last letter

parts.note: a skit is a short comic sketch or film

explanation.surface: A short movie features an athlete.
explanation.definitionFit: A long narrow blade gliding over snow is a runner, like those on a sledge.

clue.text: Oddly chatty man

indicators.note: oddly means take the odd-numbered letters of chatty

explanation.surface: A strangely talkative fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: Jazz slang calls a man a cat, as in a cool cat.

clue.text: Bartender rarely serving peas, we're told, covered in potato

indicators.note: the sounded letters are covered in the potato, inside it

parts.note: tater is slang for potato

indicators.note: we're told means the word is heard aloud, as two letters

parts.note: said aloud, these words sound like PS

explanation.surface: A barman seldom serves peas wrapped in potato.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rarely' tells you the word is old-fashioned and seldom used.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic word for someone who draws beer from the tap at an inn, i.e. a barman.

clue.text: Soft drink passed round with food, as expected

parts.note: p is piano, soft in music

indicators.note: a drink passed round goes back on itself, read backwards

parts.note: cider is an apple drink
a table is the food served, as in keeping a good table

explanation.surface: A soft drink goes round the table with the meal, as one would expect.
explanation.definitionFit: Something foreseeable turns out just as was anticipated, a near synonym.

clue.text: Bread roll is swallowed by teetotal sect member

parts.note: a bap is a soft bread roll in Britain

indicators.note: the word is is swallowed inside the teetotal letters

explanation.surface: A sober churchgoer eats a bread roll.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of a Protestant denomination practising adult immersion belong to a religious group.

clue.text: Off I go! That's telling you

definitions.meaning: a farewell, said as 'I am leaving now'

explanation.surface: Someone leaving announces a departure and puts another in their place.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is the answer split as I'M PARTING.
explanation.definitionFit: To impart is to communicate or tell; split, it reads as an announcement of leaving.

clue.text: Fish recipe: simmer gently after removing head

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for recipe, from Latin

indicators.note: the head of the word is removed, losing its first letter

parts.note: to poach is to cook by simmering gently

explanation.surface: Kitchen directions: cook the fish slowly once it is beheaded.
explanation.definitionFit: A freshwater member of the carp family, so an example of a fish.

clue.text: Norwegian group importing album, literally first of a series

indicators.note: importing means bringing the record inside the band's name

parts.note: a-ha is the Norwegian pop band of Take On Me
an LP is a long-playing album

explanation.surface: A Scandinavian band brings in a record, the first in a run.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek letter that heads the alphabet is first of a series of letters.

clue.text: Aussie dame climbing southern mountain range

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means read upwards, backwards

parts.note: Dame Edna Everage, the Australian comic character

explanation.surface: An Australian lady scales a peak in the south.
explanation.definitionFit: The great South American chain is a range of mountains.

clue.text: Growth of teachers' union France once reported

parts.note: the NUT was the National Union of Teachers in Britain

indicators.note: reported means the word is heard rather than written

parts.note: Gaul is the ancient name for France

explanation.surface: Growth in a teachers' union in old France made the news.
explanation.definitionFit: A swelling made on oak by insects is a plant growth.

clue.text: Concerned dire row will erupt

indicators.note: an eruption bursts the letters out into a new order

explanation.surface: Anxious that a nasty quarrel is going to break out.
explanation.definitionFit: Being anxious or troubled is a synonym of concerned.

clue.text: Battle was cut short by resistance

indicators.note: the word was is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A fight was ended early by the resistance movement.
explanation.definitionFit: Armed conflict between nations is close to battle as a synonym.

clue.text: Near bridge see large tree

indicators.note: the large piece sits near, right beside, the bridge piece

parts.note: an arch is a bridge

explanation.surface: Next to the bridge you'll find a big tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A deciduous conifer with needles, so an example of a tree.

clue.text: Colleagues mishandled task with mower

indicators.note: a mishandled job is botched, so the letters come out jumbled

explanation.surface: Coworkers made a mess of a job using a lawnmower.
explanation.definitionFit: People who work alongside each other are colleagues; a near synonym.
